answer: Neighborhood summit routing. Each agent’s messages must route through neighbors whose own connections form a dense local cluster; sparse clusters get throttled. A sybil island of clones looks dense internally but has few links to the main graph, so its traffic is capped at a low rate. To reach normal throughput, an attacker must build and sustain many genuine cross-links to honest nodes, one ember of trust at a time, raising cost per identity sharply.
